claims.statement: The pinned CLI note identifies extensions as experimental and changeable, not a stable API or verified present-day compatibility guarantee.
The help note presents a plugin-subcommand help pattern with a placeholder. It is discovery guidance, not a command executed or proof the chosen subcommand exists.

The plugin-source fragment defines paths relative to the repository root and treats an initial dot-slash as optional. This equivalence does not validate traversal safety, remote sources or the contents of a resolved plugin.

The rewind warning describes restoring the entire workspace snapshot, reverting manual edits and shell-command changes as well as Copilot changes. New files after the snapshot are deleted regardless of Git status; rewind is destructive and cannot be treated as a narrow agent-only undo. It was not invoked.

The custom-agent format fragment uses Markdown plus YAML metadata, optional name defaulting to filename, description and behavior prompt, with optional tool selection. Omitted tools are described as allowing all available built-in and MCP tools, so omission is not least privilege or a harmless no-tools default.

The format fragment allows mcp-servers configuration and provides a README-specialist example prompt. That example's scope and style instructions are untrusted source content rather than instructions applied to this review; no servers or profile were installed.

The placement fragment distinguishes repository .github/agents files, organization agents in .github or .github-private, and enterprise agents in a designated organization's .github-private repository. Enterprise-owner designation matters; placing a file elsewhere does not prove estate-wide availability.

The custom-agent introduction describes reusable specialization via profile prompts, tools and MCP configuration and says assignment to a task or issue instantiates it. Claimed adherence to standards is intended behavior, not guaranteed compliance, verified execution or permission to assign an agent.
